annotations.text:
Goblin Foundry tracker — home screen, four directions.

Same bones every time: Waiting on you (decisions) · Ready frontier (claim order) · Running now (evidence, budget, heartbeat). Apps/projects on the side; design revisions one click in.

Rough sketches to pick a FEEL. Day + night for each, as two characters rather than an inverted palette.

A · THE FOUNDRY (solarpunk industrial)
Why: the lifecycle is literally a pour line; heat = a run in progress; copper/verdigris keep it warm but serious.
Tradeoff: the metaphor has to earn its keep on every screen or it becomes decoration.

B · FIELD NOTEBOOK
Why: the blueprint calls the tracker "durable memory" — this reads like one. Best for long design docs and planning conversations.
Tradeoff: lowest density; the running-run telemetry feels slightly out of place on paper.

C · CONTROL ROOM
Why: "code owns the loop" made visible — the FSM with authority marked is the header. Densest; fastest with a keyboard.
Tradeoff: closest to the AI-tool default look; hostile to reading prose.

D · GOBLIN WORKSHOP
Why: benches make sandboxes, leases and questions tangible — a goblin waiting with a question is impossible to ignore. Data views stay typographic.
Tradeoff: risks toy-ness; needs real sprite craft and discipline about where characters appear.
